skill.name: list-segment-builder
skill.description: Use when the user asks to "build email segments from my list", "make engaged / lapsed / RFM segments", "set up cart-abandoner or lifecycle-stage audiences", or "build a suppression list of unsubscribes and bounces"; turns the user's OWN list/CRM/GA4/ecommerce export into behavioral, attribute, and lifecycle-stage segments plus a suppression list, with per-segment sizes labeled Measured/Estimated, informing the SEND E (Engagement/targeting) dimension. Not for scoring EQS or running vetoes — use email-quality-auditor; not for authentication or spam-content checks — use deliverability-qa. 邮件列表分群/生命周期分群/抑制名单/流失召回
skill.summary: Builds email list segments, lifecycle stages, RFM tiers, and suppression rules from owned exports.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown false positives from code fences, inline path literals, or relative repository links. One real medium-risk issue remains: the Resend connector command can read ESP data and mutate suppression state when run with --live, although the skill documents dry-run behavior. No prompt injection attempt or malicious exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Live Resend sync can mutate ESP contact state.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before --live, run a dry-run first, and document required credentials and audit logging.

remediation.issue: Saved report filenames may include user-provided list or goal text.
remediation.suggestion: Sanitize the <list-or-goal> filename component to letters, numbers, and hyphens before saving under memory/email/list-segment-builder/.

content.value_statement: Messy email exports make targeting risky and suppression rules easy to miss. This skill turns owned list data into reusable segments, lifecycle stages, and do-not-mail groups.
actual_capabilities: Profiles list, CRM, ESP, GA4, and ecommerce exports for available segmentation columns.
Builds behavioral segments such as engaged, lapsed, cart-abandoner, and clicked-no-purchase groups.
Maps customers into RFM tiers when recency, frequency, and monetary fields exist.
Creates lifecycle-stage definitions from new subscriber through win-back candidate.
Assembles suppression groups from unsubscribe, hard bounce, complaint, and consent withdrawal signals.
Labels segment sizes as measured or estimated and states the method used.
limitations: Requires owned exports or pasted columns; it does not independently access private ESP data.
Does not send campaigns, write creative, or design automated flows.
Does not score EQS or run email quality veto checks.
Cannot infer consent when registry data or opt-in fields are missing.

use_cases.title: Plan retention audiences
use_cases.description: Turn recent engagement and purchase data into active, at-risk, lapsed, and win-back groups.

use_cases.title: Prepare ecommerce campaign targets
use_cases.description: Build cart-abandoner, browse-abandon, clicked-no-purchase, and high-value buyer segments from owned exports.

use_cases.title: Check suppression coverage
use_cases.description: Create do-not-mail groups from unsubscribe, bounce, complaint, and consent withdrawal fields before launch.

prompt_templates.title: Create basic segments
prompt_templates.prompt: Build email segments from my owned list export. Goal: retention. Columns available: [paste column names]. Include suppression groups.

prompt_templates.title: Add ecommerce behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my ESP and ecommerce exports to create engaged-90d, cart-abandoner-7d, lapsed, and clicked-no-purchase segments. Label each size measured or estimated.

prompt_templates.title: Build RFM lifecycle map
prompt_templates.prompt: Map this CRM and order export into RFM tiers and lifecycle stages. Flag missing fields as NEEDS_INPUT and avoid raw PII in the output.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare campaign handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reusable segment map for a promo launch. Reconcile suppression rules with consent records, summarize SEND E relevance, and recommend the next skill.

output_examples.input: A retention marketer provides an ESP export with last open, last click, opt-in status, and bounce flags.
output_examples.output: The skill returns engaged-90d, cooling, lapsed, and suppression groups with measured counts and missing consent notes.

output_examples.input: An ecommerce operator provides order recency, order count, lifetime value, and cart activity fields.
output_examples.output: The skill produces RFM tiers, cart-abandoner groups, high-value buyer segments, and lifecycle stage definitions.

output_examples.input: A compliance lead asks which subscribers must be excluded before a promotional send.
output_examples.output: The skill summarizes do-not-mail cohorts by unsubscribe, hard bounce, complaint, and consent withdrawal status without exposing raw PII.

best_practices: Use owned exports and remove raw email addresses before sharing examples.
Check consent and suppression records before treating any cohort as mailable.
Name each segment with the source column, rule, and measured or estimated size.
anti_patterns: Do not infer opt-in status from engagement alone.
Do not paste raw subscriber rows when aggregate counts answer the question.
Do not use this skill to send campaigns or bypass ESP suppression controls.

faq.question: Does this skill send email campaigns?
faq.answer: No. It defines audiences and suppression groups only. Use another email skill or ESP workflow to send campaigns.

faq.question: What data should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide owned list, CRM, ESP, GA4, or ecommerce exports with column names and aggregate counts when possible.

faq.question: Can it build RFM segments?
faq.answer: Yes, when recency, frequency, and monetary fields are available. Missing fields are marked as NEEDS_INPUT.

faq.question: How does it handle consent?
faq.answer: It reads consent and suppression facts, then flags missing records instead of assuming a subscriber is opted in.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible skill hosts.

faq.question: Can it sync segments to an ESP?
faq.answer: Only as an optional downstream step. Resend sync commands are dry-run by default and require confirmation for live changes.
